p: Out on the west Cumbrian coast, a little preparation goes a long way, especially if you're travelling in from elsewhere in the county. Book your slot before you set off rather than turning up hoping for a space, and plan on a couple of hours for the whole visit, including check-in, harness fitting and the safety briefing.

Everyone climbing will need a participation form, signed by a parent or guardian for under-18s, so fill it in online beforehand. Have a look at the age guidance when you book, as there's usually a minimum age for climbers and supervision rules for little ones.

On the walls, the trick is to warm up on easier challenges, then work up to the scary ones. Anyone feeling nervous should try a low climb and an early let-go first. Seeing how gently the auto-belay lowers you is the best confidence booster going.

Maryport itself has a couple of hidden gems. The Lake District Coast Aquarium sits by the harbour and focuses on the sea life of the Solway and the Irish Sea, which makes it an ideal partner for a wet day. The long sandy beach at Allonby is just up the coast for a blow-out walk. Inland, Cockermouth is a short drive away, with independent shops, places to eat and Wordsworth House, the childhood home of the poet, now run by the National Trust.
